findings.evidence: The slope argument uses nonnegative intersection degree of an effective divisor with L_infty. The item asserts this but does not apply an exact intersection result. The A-page has an intersection-theory page prerequisite, but the proof should spell out the application: use Bezout for components other than L_infty and compute L_infty squared as 1 for a component equal to L_infty, then add with multiplicity.

The proof tensors the diagonal Koszul resolution by E(-1), and later by an S-flat family whose fibers are only torsion-free. The cited Koszul supplier establishes the diagonal resolution and tensor exactness for a vector bundle; it does not establish exactness after tensoring by this non-locally-free sheaf. Prove relative purity, for example from flatness of the diagonal over the first projection and flatness of the Koszul terms, or give a local coordinate-difference argument before using the spectral sequence.

The proof excludes finite-length torsion by asserting that a nonzero finite-length submodule forces depth zero, but supplies no argument or exact supplier for this fact. A nonzero socle element gives a nonzero map from the residue field and hence depth zero.

The proof concludes T_P2(-3) is stable of slope -3/2 without computing its degree from the Euler sequence. Also, stability controls only rank-one proper subsheaves, while the image of E to T_P2(-3) can have rank two. Compute deg T_P2(-3) = -3 and apply the full-rank subsheaf bound from step 2.1, as well as the rank-one stability bound, to justify the claimed contradiction.

For an arbitrary finite-type ADHM data family, the proof asserts 0 -> V O(-1) -> K -> E -> 0 is exact after citing only the fiberwise monad result. Total-space injectivity of alpha is needed before the residue-field Tor and flatness arguments, but is not established. Prove it locally from the explicit matrix, for example using an appropriate monic block determinant on each standard chart, or cite and verify a relative exactness criterion.
